title: Driveways
shortDesc: Five inches on every driveway. Never four. Compacted 21AA under the slab.
fullDesc: {{name}} pours driveways in {{region}}. The slab is five inches, every time. The estimate names that thickness and the 21AA base.
heading: Five inches, not four
body: Most contractors pour four inches. Skipping that inch is how a bid gets cheaper. {{name}} charges for the inch and pours it. The finishers have been finishing concrete for more than 25 years.

faq.a: Michigan cold and a heavy delivery truck work on a thin slab. Five inches is the driveway. Six inches is the approach.

title: Driveway approaches
shortDesc: Six inches where the street meets the drive, on the same compacted 21AA base.
fullDesc: {{name}} pours the approach at six inches. That is the section a 20-ton delivery truck hits first.
heading: The approach is thicker
body: The approach is its own thickness because that is where the weight from the street lands. It is still graded and compacted 21AA before anyone sets a form.

faq.q: Is the approach included with a driveway?
faq.a: When we pour the driveway, the approach is part of the spec: six inches there, five on the rest.

title: Flatwork
shortDesc: Pads and other slabs poured to the same spec as a driveway.
fullDesc: {{name}} pours flatwork to the driveway spec: five inches, six where it is an approach, compacted 21AA.
highlights: Never four to win the bid
A specialist, not a side job
heading: Flatwork, not a side hobby
body: Concrete is its own company here. The flatwork is not a cheaper four-inch pour. Finishers with more than 25 years do the surface you live with.

faq.q: Is flatwork poured thinner than a driveway?
faq.a: No. Five inches, every time, unless the section is an approach. Approaches are six.

title: Stamped concrete
shortDesc: Stamped patterns on the same five-inch slab and compacted 21AA base.
fullDesc: {{name}} stamps concrete to the same spec as a plain driveway: five inches, six on an approach, compacted 21AA. Pattern photos on this site are illustrations, not finished jobs.
heading: A pattern on the same slab
body: The stamp is the finish. The body of the slab is still five inches over compacted 21AA. Pavers are part of the work too. This site does not have a paver pattern board yet.

faq.q: Are the pattern photos your jobs?
faq.a: No. They are AI illustrations of pattern and color, so you can see the options. They are not photos of a completed Faber Concrete job.
